authority: New prospective noncircular field-witness design plus exact numerical examples. No pickup data, chip layout or implemented h-CQUID instrument is claimed.

primaryPrecedent.result: Independent on-chip SQUID-resonator flux-to-microwave-phase transduction, without using a qubit transition matrix element.
primaryPrecedent.bandwidthBoundary: The paper demonstrates waveforms through hundreds of MHz and describes a 2.6 GHz bandwidth limit. Precision for the proposed 1.8-2.56 GHz h-CQUID carrier range must be independently demonstrated, not assumed from the nominal bandwidth.

rejectedShortcuts: Matching qubit Rabi amplitudes or Stark shifts using an assumed current matrix element is circular for this test.
An ordinary first-order longitudinal Ramsey flux meter is blind at the exact flux-degeneracy reference where the static frequency slope vanishes.
A second measurement of remote transmission or input power alone does not identify local flux under unknown reflected and screening currents.

proposedWitness.hardware: A weakly loading on-chip flux pickup/SQUID transducer coupled to the relevant drive-current modes, with a separate probe carrier. A pickup of only a remote feedline is insufficient without a transfer/coverage proof.
proposedWitness.measurement: While switching the h-CQUID between paired working points, keep the pump carrier and source waveform fixed and keep the sensor at the same operating point. Measure its complex probe carrier C and pump-induced sideband B.
proposedWitness.smallSignalModel: B_b/C_b=K(omega_p) Phi_sensor,b + O(Phi_sensor,b^3), b=target,reference. Sensor and detector gain K need not be absolutely known if it is unchanged within each interleaved pair.
proposedWitness.selfReferencedObservable: R_sensor=(B_target C_reference)/(B_reference C_target)=Phi_sensor,target/Phi_sensor,reference in the linear regime.
proposedWitness.gainCancellation: An unknown sensor response and different gains at the probe carrier and sideband cancel because each frequency bin appears in both blocks. A blockwise common probe-amplitude/gain factor also cancels.
proposedWitness.notCancelled: State-correlated change of sensor operating point, carrier/sideband gain ratio, crosstalk, or a spatial flux component not seen by the pickup.
proposedWitness.operatingPointControl: Hold the sensor DC response fixed; interleave blocks faster than drift. Use an independent small calibration dither and probe-power checks to test sensor-gain invariance, not the qubit matrix element.
proposedWitness.backactionControl: Bound sensor-induced shifts, heating, poisoning and changes in coherence by sensor-probe-power and sensor-on/off controls. Freeze the static spectrum of the instrumented device before acquiring the strength test.
proposedWitness.nonlinearityControl: Repeat at several small pump amplitudes. The leading cross-ratio is amplitude independent; retain nonlinear corrections or restrict the regime using the witness data, not by fitting a qubit strength correction.

localityCriterion.model: Let relevant physical drive/screening mode currents be i, device flux Phi_D=m_D^T i, and sensor fluxes phi_S=M_S i.
localityCriterion.identifiability: Device flux is reconstructible from the sensors if and only if m_D^T is in the row span of M_S, on the allowed current subspace.
localityCriterion.reconstruction: Choose a such that a^T M_S=m_D^T; then Phi_D=a^T phi_S. An unknown overall common calibration scale cancels in target/reference ratios; relative sensor calibrations and the coupling geometry still need to be fixed independently.
localityCriterion.singleModeEscape: If one measured current generates the relevant external flux through a fixed mutual inductance M, Phi_D=M I_local, the same-current ratio suffices. The M need not be known absolutely.
localityCriterion.multipleModeBoundary: Shared resonator and induced screening/return currents can require more than one independent pickup. A single scalar sensor is conclusive only if its coupling is proportional to the device-flux functional on that subspace.
localityCriterion.requiredEvidence: Circuit topology and relative mutual couplings, or an experimentally validated independent-mode injection/Maxwell reconstruction. Low-frequency coupling calibration alone does not prove a GHz mode model.

numericalCounterexample.interpretation: A single pickup reports equality while the actual device flux changes by 10 percent. A second independent mode measurement detects it; no qubit matrix element is used.

correctedStrengthTest.formula: W_target/W_reference=|Omega_target/Omega_reference|^2 / |Phi_D,target/Phi_D,reference|^2, after the Rabi damping correction in the preceding protocol.
correctedStrengthTest.equalityAlternative: Use the independent flux witness to servo the two local fields equal before acquiring Rabi traces. That is input calibration, not a fit of the strength law.
correctedStrengthTest.order: Freeze the sensor/coupling calibration and loading correction before scoring the predicted current ratios. Preserve complex field ratios and covariance.
correctedStrengthTest.remainingConditions: Linear stable readout for normalized preparation differences, identified charge/parity branch, validated pulse dynamics and independent bounds on sensor backaction and unobserved field modes.

conclusion: An independent local-flux witness can remove the circularity. The equal-field assertion is conditional on sensor stability and coverage of the device-flux modes. The public h-CQUID release contains no such witness; this requires a new measurement setup or an independently validated local-current monitor.
